prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1299; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states the other vehicle crossed into the lane during a merge. Both vehicles driven from the scene. Initial photos requested from insured and posted to file.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Representation letter received and logged. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Preservation request sent for the other vehicle's repair records and any telematics data.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck strain with stiffness and headaches since the collision. Medical records requested through counsel. No emergency treatment noted in the initial report. Reserve placed pending review of treatment notes.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. Front bumper, hood, and both headlamp assemblies show damage consistent with the reported impact speed. Repair estimate received and under review. Independent appraisal scheduled to confirm the figures before any payment is authorized.

Entry 5: Counsel's office requested a status update and an estimate of the settlement timeline. Response sent confirming the file remains open pending receipt of the medical records and the repair appraisal. Next review set for the standard diary date.
